summary: Meiji Yamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962), where he later served as a professor (attested 1963, 2007).

Meinrad Scheller was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Paris and the University of Zurich under Manu Leumann, Ernst Risch, and Julius Pokorny. He held professorships at Fribourg (1963), Munich (1968–1975), and Zurich (1975).
Meiping Li is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

Meir Shahar is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1987–1992) and became an Associate Professor of Chinese Studies at Tel Aviv University (~1994).

Melissa R. Kerin works in art history and archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter, and held a professorship at Washington and Lee University (attested 2015).

Melvyn C. Goldstein is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Washington (PhD ~1961–1968), and served as an anthropology professor at Case Western Reserve University (1968–2002).

Merab Mamardashvili was a philosopher who studied at Moscow University's Department of Philosophy (~1949–1954). He held posts at Moscow State University (~1968–1974), Top Courses for Scriptwriters and Film Directors (~1977–1980), and Tbilisi State University (1987–1990).

Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 1980), where he was supervised by Leon Hurvitz, and also studied under Kathryn Ann Adelsperger Cissell.
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel.

Michael Alram is a specialist in numismatics, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer, holding major posts at the Kunsthistorisches Museum and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Michael Aris was a Tibetologist and historian who studied at Durham University and SOAS (PhD) under David Llewellyn Snellgrove. He held positions at the University of Oxford, Wolfson College, St Antony's College, and Harvard University.
Michael Balk is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1988 and held a post at the Prussian State Library (attested 1991).

Michael Baxandall was an art historian who studied at Cambridge, Pavia, and Munich. He held appointments at the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Warburg Institute, Oxford, the Courtauld Institute of Art, Cornell University, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Michael Bernays was a scholar who studied at the University of Bonn and Heidelberg University under Adolf Holtzmann. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (1872–1873) and the University of Munich (1873–1890).

Michael Carrithers is an anthropologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Oxford, and held academic posts at Oxford, the London School of Economics, and Durham University (1982–present).

Michael Comans is an Indologist and philosopher. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University, and was a faculty member at the University of Sydney (~1988–2002).

Michael Como is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Bernard Faure, Carl Bielefeldt, and Kuo-liang Wang. He held a post at Columbia University (attested 2009).

Michael Eido Luetchford is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a degree in Electronic Engineering at the University of Bradford (~1964–1967) and studied traditionally under Gudō Wafu Nishijima (~1973–2007).

Michael Friedrich is a Sinologist who earned his PhD at the University of Munich (~1978–1984), where he also worked as an assistant (1983–1986). He served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.

Michael Hahn was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Wilhelm Rau at Marburg (PhD 1967). He held professorships at the University of Bonn (1974, 1982) and the University of Marburg (1976–1980, 1988–2007).
